overview: Supplier Lead-Time Reliability Insights addresses telemetry is noisy or missing, so operators spend time interpreting unrelated warnings in logistics and supply chain operations. The first proof of value uses purchase orders, supplier acknowledgments and receipts. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is supplier lead time variance, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: purchase orders, supplier acknowledgments and receipts; define supplier lead time variance and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Logistics COO / Supply Chain Director.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including inject sensor failures, stale data and dependency loss into the pilot.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
deliverables: Agreed test threshold for supplier lead time variance
